summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with cirrhosis from chronic hepatitis C, hepatocellular carcinoma, and type 2 diabetes, was admitted from her primary care office due to persistent hyperglycemia with blood sugars ranging from 250 to 400 despite adherence to her insulin regimen. She also reported increased lethargy and urinary frequency. Evaluation revealed patchy opacities on chest X-ray concerning for early pneumonia, and she was started on levofloxacin. Urinalysis showed bacteria, but the culture was contaminated and not actionable. Her blood glucose improved with insulin regimen adjustments managed by the diabetes team. She remained stable, with no respiratory symptoms or fever, and was discharged home on a three-day course of oral levofloxacin, continued insulin with an increased sliding scale, and discontinuation of ferrous gluconate. A visiting nurse was arranged for home support, and follow-up was scheduled with her hepatologist and primary care provider.
